LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's top-level (global) scope contains only standard variable assignments: pkgname, pkgdesc, pkgver, pkgrel, arch, url, license, groups, depends, makedepends, options, and a private _skinsdir path. The `source` array defines the package's own declared upstream download URL (aimp.ru catalog download for the Victor KD-D55 AIMP skin), which is expected for this package type and involves no execution at this stage. The `noextract=("${source[@]%%::*}")` line performs a pure bash string-parameter expansion to strip the URL from the filename — a harmless text operation with no command substitution, eval, network access, or file writes.

No command substitutions (`$(...)` or backticks), `eval`, `curl`, `wget`, `base64`, or exec-style calls exist at top level. The only file operation in the file is `bsdtar -xf` inside the `package()` function, which does not execute during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` (function bodies are not sourced/run at this gate). The URL points to the upstream aimp.ru download endpoint, consistent with the package's stated purpose of distributing an AIMP skin.

This is a minimal, standard binary-packaging PKGBUILD with no supply-chain attack indicators in the portion executed by the narrow gate.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Top-level scope only has normal variable definitions; no malicious executable code.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This .SRCINFO file defines metadata for the aimp-skin-victor-kd-d55 AUR package. The source is downloaded from aimp.ru (the official AIMP website) at `https://aimp.ru/?do=catalog.download&id=667`, which is expected for an AIMP skin package. The `noextract` directive prevents automatic extraction during build, which is a legitimate packaging choice when the build() function handles extraction manually. The `makedepends = libarchive` dependency supports archive extraction. No malicious patterns are present: no eval, no unexpected network calls, no obfuscated code, no exfiltration attempts. The only minor concern is the `sha256sums` value appears to be a SHA-1 hash (40 hex characters) rather than a SHA-256 hash (64 hex characters), which is a checksum hygiene issue but not evidence of malice.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>No malicious behavior detected; standard AUR skin package metadata.</summary>
